title: Changelog Generator (Model Metadata) — Technical Plan v0.6
content:
Doc purpose
- This is a working implementation plan for the “model changelog generator” pipeline (v1). It covers: pipeline stages, data flow, storage/immutability approach, failure modes, and a milestone plan mapped to current Linear issues.
- Audience: platform eng (registry/control plane), release engineering, Console backend, Docs.
- Non-goal: finalize schema fields. Assume schema_v1 exists + registry emits change-events with actor/timestamp/event_id.

Background / problem statement
- Today model updates are communicated inconsistently (docs page edits, Slack, occasional runtime release notes). Customers report “behavior changed without notice” during rollouts and pinned versions.
- Desired state: a single source-of-truth change-event stream (from model registry) that produces customer-visible release notes (docs + Console + API/SDK linkouts) with an approval workflow and audit trail.

High-level architecture (v1)
- Source of truth: Model Registry Metadata Service emits signed change-events for create/update/deprecate operations.
- Generator: stateless worker(s) consume change-events, compute canonical diffs, render “customer-safe” drafts, and persist drafts for review.
- Review + publish: Drafts move through state machine (draft -> in_review -> published). Publication writes immutable changelog entries and triggers docs publish job + makes entry available via Console APIs and feed endpoints.
- Audit: every stage produces audit events with actor and event correlation IDs.

Key concepts / data model (terminology)
- change_event: immutable event emitted by registry with event_id, model_id, version_id, operation, actor, timestamp, and “before/after” (or patch) payload.
- change_diff: derived, normalized representation of what changed (field-level). Deterministic ordering; used for templating, redaction, and display.
- changelog_draft: editable artifact (customer-visible text + structured sections) created by generator.
- changelog_entry: immutable published artifact associated with one or more change_events (see “batching / collapsing” section).
- public_changelog_fields allowlist: explicit list of fields allowed to influence customer-visible output (to prevent leaks).

Pipeline stages

Stage 0 — Event ingestion
Inputs
- Model registry change-events (create/update/deprecate) emitted on:
  - model version creation
  - metadata updates
  - deprecation/unsupport operations
Assumptions
- Events include: event_id (UUIDv7 preferred for ordering), actor_id, actor_type (user/service), occurred_at, model_id, version_id, schema_version, and signed payload.
- Delivery semantics: at-least-once.
Implementation sketch
- Consumer service subscribes to event stream (internal bus). Persist raw events to “event store” for replay.
- Deduplicate by event_id.
- Validate signature + schema_version compatibility.

Stage 1 — Diff detection + normalization
Goal
- Convert raw event payload into canonical diff for templating + downstream display.
Rules
- Deterministic diff ordering: sort by (model_id, version_id, occurred_at, event_id). Do not rely solely on timestamps.
- Normalize fields:
  - version identifiers: ensure model_id/version_id standard form
  - deployment compatibility: Hosted/Dedicated/Private matrix normalized into stable ordering
  - numeric metrics (latency/throughput/cost) stored as structured “observed metrics” + optional links
- Compute “change categories” (taxonomy):
  - new_model_version
  - performance
  - compatibility
  - safety_policy
  - bugfix
  - deprecation
  - documentation_only (ideally suppressed from customer release notes unless explicitly approved)
Notes
- We should aim to keep diff logic pure + unit-testable. (We’ve already seen staging issues where multiple updates in a day collapse incorrectly.)

Stage 2 — Redaction + public field allowlist
Goal
- Ensure generator never leaks internal-only fields (internal nicknames, vendor-specific notes, non-public eval prompts, capacity notes, internal incident refs).
Mechanism
- Use a strict allowlist of “public-changelog-influencing” fields.
- If an event changes only non-public fields: generate a draft marked “internal-only change; do not publish” OR suppress draft creation entirely (TBD by PM/Docs).
- Additionally, apply string redaction checks:
  - blocklisted tokens: internal model codenames, cluster names, vendor account IDs
  - URL allowlist: only docs.redwood… + console.redwood… + approved eval dashboard domains
- Any redaction-trigger should create a review-required flag and emit an audit log event.

Stage 3 — Draft rendering (templating)
Outputs
- changelog_draft with:
  - customer_safe_summary (1–3 sentences)
  - sections: Impact, Compatibility, Known Issues (if any), Deprecation timeline (if applicable), Links
  - machine-readable metadata: model_id, version_id, categories, affected_deployments, created_from_event_ids
Templating rules (v1)
- Always include Compatibility section even if “No change.” (Avoid ambiguity.)
- If perf metrics are present, display as directional and scoped (e.g., “Lower median latency for short prompts on A100 class GPUs”) and link to dashboards; do not expose internal benchmark harness names.
- If change is a deprecation:
  - must include sunset_date and replacement_model (if known)
  - must include customer action required vs no action
- Ensure language is customer-safe:
  - no blame language
  - avoid “we changed kernels / compiler flags” unless it has customer-impact framing
- Drafts are created in “draft” state and require human review to publish.

Stage 4 — Review workflow + approvals
State machine
- draft: created by generator; editable by allowed internal roles
- in_review: reviewer assigned; content locked except for reviewers
- published: immutable, customer-visible
- superseded: published entry replaced by corrective entry; original remains visible via audit history / “superseded by” link
Roles (initial)
- Editors: can edit drafts (Product + Release Eng + Docs + designated Eng)
- Approvers/Publishers: restricted (Release Eng + Product lead; add Compliance/Security approver for certain categories)
- Emergency publish path:
  - allowed only for Release Eng on-call during incident/hotfix window
  - requires post-hoc review within 1 business day
Review SLA targets (draft proposal)
- Routine updates: <= 2 business days to publish
- Deprecations: publish same day as internal announcement (ideally before rollout)
- Hotfix correction: <= 4 hours

Stage 5 — Publication targets
Targets
1) Control plane API (Console)
- Read endpoints:
  - list by model_id (filter by date/category)
  - list by version_id
  - fetch by entry_id
- Pagination: cursor-based; stable ordering by published_at then entry_id.
- Feature flag + account-tier gating handled at API layer.

2) Docs site publish
- Docs consumes “published feed” artifact and generates per-model landing pages + global changelog + RSS/Atom.
- Docs publish job should be idempotent; break-glass rollback if docs deploy fails.
- Ensure canonical URLs are stable and referenced by API/SDK (changelog_url).

3) Public feed endpoint (machine-readable)
- JSON feed with ETags + caching. Rate-limited.
- NOTE: v1 is batch/daily acceptable. Real-time streaming not required.

Stage 6 — Observability + operational ownership
Metrics (minimum)
- publish_lag_seconds: time from event occurred_at to published_at
- draft_backlog_count: drafts older than SLA
- validation_failures_total (by reason)
- redaction_triggers_total
- docs_publish_failures_total
- feed_generation_latency
Tracing
- Correlate end-to-end with correlation_id = event_id (or derived batch id) across registry -> generator -> publish -> docs.
Alerts (initial)
- “Publish lag p95 > 24h” (warning) and > 72h (page)
- Docs publish failures > 3 in 1h (page)
- Validation failure spike (warning)

Data flow diagram (text)

[Model Registry] 
   | emits change_event (signed)
   v
[Event Bus]  ---> (dead-letter topic on validation/signature failure)
   |
   v
[Generator Consumer]
   | persist raw event
   v
[Event Store] (append-only)
   |
   v
[Diff + Redaction]
   |
   v
[Draft Store] --(workflow edits/review)--> [Approval API]
   |
   | on publish
   v
[Published Changelog Store] (immutable; supports supersede)
   |                 |
   |                 +--> [Docs Publish Job] --> [Docs Site + RSS]
   |
   +--> [Console API] / [Public Feed API]

Batching / collapsing logic (open but needs a decision)
Problem
- Multiple updates to the same model/version can occur within hours (metadata correction + compatibility addition + deprecation message tweak). Customers should not see noisy spam, but we must preserve auditability.
Proposed v1 approach
- Draft creation: one draft per change_event initially.
- “Auto-batch” window for publication: when publishing, allow the reviewer to merge multiple drafts into a single published entry (still references all event_ids).
- Published entries remain immutable; if an error exists, publish a corrective “superseding” entry rather than editing in place.
Reasoning
- Minimizes accidental collapsing bugs and maintains a clean audit chain.

Storage + immutability notes
- Event Store: append-only; retention >= 2 years (TBD by security/compliance). Prefer WORM-ish semantics (object lock) if feasible.
- Published Changelog Store: treat as immutable records; supports supersede pointers.
- Draft Store: mutable; retains edit history with actor/time for audit.
- All stores include: tenant scope (if any), environment (staging/prod), and schema version.

Validation + failure modes
1) Event schema validation error
- Action: reject event; write to DLQ; alert if rate increases.
- Operator runbook: inspect DLQ payload; coordinate with registry team.

2) Redaction triggered
- Action: create draft but mark “requires security/docs review”; do not auto-publish.

3) Docs publish failure
- Action: keep published changelog entry available via API; retry docs job; alert if repeated.
- Ensure docs URLs only get surfaced once docs publish succeeds OR use a stable redirector that can return 202 until ready.

4) Wrong/ambiguous customer wording
- Action: publish superseding correction entry. Original remains, marked superseded.

Milestones (rough) mapped to Linear
Phase 1: Core ingestion + drafts (platform)
- ENG-4923: change-event emission in registry (diff format, event IDs, audit fields)
- ENG-4926 (part): generator worker consumes events and creates drafts
- ENG-4932: RBAC foundation for who can edit/approve
Deliverable
- Internal-only drafts viewable in admin UI or via API; no docs/Console exposure yet.

Phase 2: Approval + publish + Console integration (control plane + console)
- redwood PR: approval workflow endpoints (draft -> in_review -> published)
- ENG-4927: Console changelog tab behind feature flag
- ENG-4928: API contract: model_version + changelog_url surfaced in responses/headers
Deliverable
- Selected internal users can publish entries; Console can display published entries for beta accounts.

Phase 3: Docs + feeds + observability + hardening
- Docs site generation and navigation
- Public feed endpoint with caching/ETags
- ENG-4930: dashboards + alerting for publish lag and pipeline failures
Deliverable
- End-to-end GA readiness: published entries visible in Console + docs + feed; operational runbook.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Batching policy: auto-merge window vs manual merge only (see batching section)
- Required reviewers for “safety/policy” category: do we require Compliance + Security co-approval or only for certain tags?
- URL strategy: ensure changelog_url is stable even if docs deploy lags (redirector vs delayed exposure).
- Tenant visibility: do we ever need per-customer suppression? (Out of scope for v1, but avoid blocking future.)
- Backfill: how far back do we generate “historical” changelog entries during migration? (Support wants at least top models for last 90 days; TBD.)

Immediate next steps (next 1–2 weeks)
- Align on canonical diff format + deterministic ordering constraints with registry team (ENG-4923 dependencies).
- Finalize allowlist for public fields + redaction rules (Docs + Security sign-off).
- Implement minimal draft schema + endpoints for listing drafts and marking in_review.
- Define initial templates for 5 categories (new version, perf, compatibility, deprecation, bugfix) and run them against staging events.

Appendix: example draft template (placeholder)
Title: <Model Name> <version_id> — <Category>
Date: <published_at>
Summary: <customer_safe_summary>
Impact:
- <bullet 1>
Compatibility:
- Hosted: <...>
- Dedicated: <...>
- Private: <...>
Deprecation (if applicable):
- Sunset date: <...>
- Replacement: <...>
Links:
- Changelog entry: <url>
- Evals/metrics: <url>

Notes to self
- Keep generator worker stateless; avoid coupling to docs build internals.
- Don’t bake in “OpenAI route names” into templates; keep API-agnostic and let Console/Docs decide UI labeling.
- Ensure every published entry references event_ids for audit and troubleshooting.
